text.style: font-size: 16px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #111111

g.text: Expected height of boys and girls, from birth to age 19

text.style: font-size: 10.5px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', sans-serif; fill: #555555

g.text: The bands show the range of heights among children of the same age in the World Health Organization's growth reference

text.style: font-size: 10.5px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', sans-serif; fill: #555555

g.text: population: the middle 50% spans the 25th to 75th percentile, the middle 80% the 10th to 90th, and the middle 94% the 3rd to

text.style: font-size: 10.5px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', sans-serif; fill: #555555

g.text: 97th. Girls are taller than boys, on average, between the ages of about 9 and 13.

text.style: font-size: 7.75px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', sans-serif; fill: #777777

g.text: Note: The curves step down slightly at age 2, where height starts being measured standing up rather than lying down, and at age 5, where WHO's standards for under-fives

text.style: font-size: 7.75px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', sans-serif; fill: #777777

g.text: give way to its reference for older children. Both steps are in the original data. The under-fives standards show how children grow in good conditions; the reference for older

text.style: font-size: 7.75px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', sans-serif; fill: #777777

g.text: children describes how an earlier sample did grow.

text.style: font-size: 7.75px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #888888

g.text: Data source: WHO Child Growth Standards (2006); WHO Growth Reference (2007)

text.style: font-size: 7.75px; font-family: 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Liberation Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #888888

g.text: OurWorldinData.org — Research and data to make progress against the world's largest problems.
